title: Nirnay: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The OMR Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The OMR Sheet
options.lineage: Indian competitive-exam OMR response sheets, marked in examiner's red
options.thesis: Every ticket is a response sheet: bubbles filled to confidence, judged in examiner's red, checked against the answer key.
options.viewport: The queue is a stack of response sheets down a timing-mark rail; the open ticket shows six category bubbles filled to confidence, the reply in the answer box, and the examiner's verdict with reasons in the margin.
options.risk: Tips into costume if the bubbles and marks are decoration rather than real, scannable controls.

raised.raise: The sheet's timing-mark track and registration corners are the real layout grid; every queue row lands on a timing mark.
The confidence threshold is a draggable line across every bubble scale and the answer-key chart; moving it re-marks the test set live.
Reading and writing are one object: the drafted reply is edited in place in the answer box and approved with one keystroke.
State is never colour alone: tick, circle and starred-circle marks carry auto-reply, escalate and urgent in shape and words.
Total ink commitment: drop-out blue prints all structure at full strength instead of a timid accent.

options.label: The Government File Noting
options.lineage: Indian government files: green noting sheets, buff covers, 'put up for decision' flags
options.thesis: Each ticket is a file that moves up the desk with a written noting until someone records the decision.
options.viewport: A file register on the left, the open file's noting sheet in the centre with each step's note and signature, and the decision recorded at the foot.
options.risk: Evokes red tape and slowness, the opposite of fast support, and drifts toward the familiar warm-paper look.

options.label: Starship Wall Panel
options.thesis: Colour banks you travel between, framed by sweeping elbows.
options.viewport: Elbow frame with categories as pastel pill banks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: support agents don't identify with sci-fi consoles, and pastel-on-black hurts long reply reading.
options.risk: Reads as fandom costume in a work tool.
options.kept: The frame itself is the layout grid.

options.label: Yé-yé Record Sleeve
options.thesis: One saturated ground per release, four tracks in a tidy corner.
options.viewport: Flat tangerine ground with the ticket as the portrait.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dense queue is not a four-track release; no audience link.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscopes on a signal bench
options.thesis: Every signal measured against one graticule; the trigger level holds it still.
options.viewport: Threshold sweep as a trace with a draggable trigger line.
options.case: Fuses well only for the threshold chart; loses on audience and on reading reply text.
options.kept: The threshold as a draggable trigger line, measured on one scale.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Cards you read and edit with the same hand.
options.viewport: Each ticket a card; the reply editable in place.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience link, and one-bit can't carry confidence or urgency.
options.kept: Browse and author are one object.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis rules every line.
options.viewport: Queue as a descent, urgent tickets at depth.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in a support shift maps to depth.
options.kept: A single axis rules every line.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Named light phases, never colour alone.
options.case: Fuses poorly: lighting cues don't match queue work; no audience link.
options.kept: Every state named, never colour alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern helpdesk (Zendesk / Intercom / Linear style), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, ticket list, detail pane with a reply composer and a status sidebar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every helpdesk by design.
